Q: How can I compact a bit pattern by removing every other bit in C? A:

If you allocate a little memory, then packing a 32-bit number can be done in 13 operations:

#include <stdint.h>

uint32_t m[0xAA + 1] = {
    // odd
    [0b00000000] = 0b0000, [0b10000000] = 0b1000,
    [0b00000010] = 0b0001, [0b10000010] = 0b1001,
    [0b00001000] = 0b0010, [0b10001000] = 0b1010, 
    [0b00001010] = 0b0011, [0b10001010] = 0b1011, 
    [0b00100000] = 0b0100, [0b10100000] = 0b1100, 
    [0b00100010] = 0b0101, [0b10100010] = 0b1101, 
    [0b00101000] = 0b0110, [0b10101000] = 0b1110, 
    [0b00101010] = 0b0111, [0b10101010] = 0b1111,    
    // even
    [0b00000000] = 0b0000, [0b01000000] = 0b1000,
    [0b00000001] = 0b0001, [0b01000001] = 0b1001,
    [0b00000100] = 0b0010, [0b01000100] = 0b1010, 
    [0b00000101] = 0b0011, [0b01000101] = 0b1011, 
    [0b00010000] = 0b0100, [0b01010000] = 0b1100, 
    [0b00010001] = 0b0101, [0b01010001] = 0b1101, 
    [0b00010100] = 0b0110, [0b01010100] = 0b1110, 
    [0b00010101] = 0b0111, [0b01010101] = 0b1111 };

#define PACK_BITS(m, x, y) \
    ((m)[((x)      ) & (y)]      ) \
  | ((m)[((x) >>  8) & (y)] <<  4) \
  | ((m)[((x) >> 16) & (y)] <<  8) \
  | ((m)[((x) >> 24) & (y)] << 12)

uint32_t pack_odd (uint32_t x) { return PACK_BITS(m, x, 0xAA); }
uint32_t pack_even(uint32_t x) { return PACK_BITS(m, x, 0x55); }
